evidence: spec.md, User Story 1: "A maintainer manually invokes f-auditor to find user-visible functional problems with the two skills across projects under their GitRepo folder."
spec.md, User Story 1 / Acceptance Scenario 1: "the auditor examines the entire session, including earlier context, for relevant skill friction."
spec.md, User Story 2: "The auditor updates it without undoing human status changes or losing edits."
spec.md, User Story 3 / Acceptance Scenario 2: "it returns an actionable, distinguishable outcome instead of claiming full success."
spec.md, FR-012: "it MUST distinguish full coverage, partial coverage, and failed runs."
spec.md, FR-011: "The system MUST assign each issue a priority using documented criteria and distinguish the rationale when the ranking is not obvious."
spec.md, FR-002: "The default audit window MUST be the 24 hours immediately preceding a single captured audit-start instant, expressed unambiguously in time."
spec.md, FR-004: "The system MUST limit eligible sessions to those reliably associated with the configured repository/folder root"
spec.md, FR-008: "The system MUST consolidate occurrences of the same underlying problem across sessions under one issue and retain the evidence for each occurrence."
spec.md, FR-010: "pre-fix evidence alone MUST NOT trigger a regression."
spec.md, FR-018: "The system MUST NOT modify the audited skills, mark issues fixed, create external issues, commit, push, or deploy as part of an audit."
spec.md, SC-002: "Every reported fixture finding contains an affected skill, actionable proposed improvement, priority, `Not Fixed` initial status, and traceable session evidence."

artifact_paths: spec.md#User Story 1 - Audit relevant recent sessions
findings.completion_criterion: Add an analysis-quality acceptance outcome using representative Hermes and Codex transcripts with explicitly expected supported problems and negative cases containing unrelated project failures or corrections resolved by surrounding context. Verify that the expected problems are discovered, their evidence and suggested improvements address the observed behavior, and negative cases do not become issues. A no-findings result on positive fixtures must fail acceptance.
evidence: spec.md, User Story 1 / Why this priority: "Without trustworthy discovery and meaningful findings, the auditor cannot deliver its purpose."

spec.md, FR-005: "The system MUST identify friction relevant to using or attempting to use `refine-idea` or `implement-refine-idea`, including user corrections, observed failures, and extra setup; unrelated project problems MUST NOT be included solely because they appeared in an eligible session."
spec.md, SC-001: "In a representative Hermes and Codex fixture suite, all eligible sessions are selected and all open, outside-root, and outside-window sessions are excluded."
spec.md, SC-002: "Every reported fixture finding contains an affected skill, actionable proposed improvement, priority, `Not Fixed` initial status, and traceable session evidence."
findings.summary: The measurable outcomes verify session selection and finding structure, but not whether contextual analysis discovers the supported functional problems. An auditor that selects every eligible session yet reports no findings can satisfy these outcomes. This leaves the feature's central value, trustworthy discovery of actionable skill friction, without an acceptance gate.

artifact_paths: spec.md#User Story 2 - Maintain the shared backlog
findings.completion_criterion: Clarify that the shared file must provide a priority-ordered presentation of actionable issues, without prescribing its representation or overriding contributor-maintained content. Add an acceptance case starting with mixed-priority issues and introducing a higher-priority finding; verify that a contributor can identify the highest-priority actionable issues directly from the file after the update while existing human edits remain intact.
evidence: spec.md, Input: "maintain a shared, prioritized functional improvement backlog."
spec.md, User Story 2: "A maintainer and other contributors use one file as the source of truth for prioritized improvements."
spec.md, FR-007: "The system MUST maintain a single shared source-of-truth issue file under `functional-improvement/`; new issues MUST start as `Not Fixed`."
spec.md, FR-011: "The system MUST assign each issue a priority using documented criteria and distinguish the rationale when the ranking is not obvious."
findings.summary: The maintainer journey promises a prioritized shared backlog, but the requirements only mandate storing issues and assigning priority labels. They do not require a priority-ordered presentation in the shared file. An append-only file with scattered priority labels could meet the stated requirements while making contributors repeatedly reconstruct what to work on first.
